title: an `_arguments` action whose text fails sh:463's eval runs its first character as a command; when that is a builtin (`r`) zsh runs it and reports `bad option: -J`, zshrs ran nothing

observed.measured: 2026-10-30, target/debug/zshrs with the dispatch_action_command builtin arm (zshrs 0.13.56) vs zsh 5.9.999.3-test (~/.cache/zshrs/zsh-oracle-new), scripts/compsys_spec_fuzz.py --spec
observed.notes: The message `pat*` ends at the first colon, so the action is `rest:(r1 r2)`. sh:463 `eval "action=( $action )"` fails (`unknown file attribute: 1`), `action` stays a scalar, and sh:465 runs `"$action[1]"` = `r`, the `fc -e -` builtin, with `$expl` (`-J ...`). Src/exec.c runs a builtin in the current shell through execbuiltin; dispatch_action_command returned 1 for every builtin without running it.

observed_when_diverging.recorded_under: target/debug/zshrs at a9add374ed before the fix (zshrs 0.13.56) vs zsh 5.9.999.3-test

why_this_fixture_exists: Found by the round-2 lane-1 `_arguments` probe `*:pat*:rest:(r1 r2)`. Any builtin reached as an action command word (sh:455 / sh:465, `_all_labels` sh:35 / sh:39) was silently treated as a failed action.
